title: Services electricity demand grows with the industrial multiple after 2023
why: M3731 (2023) uses the services multiple (row 3713); from N3731 the copied formula points six rows up, to the industrial multiple (row 3707).
ref: M3731 (2023) = L3731*M3713. Already scripted: bugfix_procedure/FixL1_ServicesElectricity.bas.
effect: 2040 services demand +29% (baseline) and +15% (carbon tax); total demand +7.7%. Excel test run of the macro: 2041 services +30.8% (baseline), +16.1% (policy).

title: Income factor on the GDP elasticity applied twice and anchored to 2023
why: Exponent = (eps_Y / $M3686) x M3686 x M2433, and M3686 already = average elasticity x M2433, so the effective elasticity is eps_Y x inc(t)^2 / inc(2023).
ref: Legacy fuel rows (e.g. 5399): (1+g)^(eps_Y x M2433), the income factor once. Row 3686 is then read by nothing; leave it as a memo row.
effect: 2040 demand +3.2% (baseline) and +3.7% (carbon tax).

title: Actual capacity factors are never used
where: Mitigation A4, rows 2999-3007 (N; Q and W follow)
why: The installed-capacity lookup N2999 searches the year header Power!F357:Y357 (2000-2019) for FirstYearCalculations (2022, column AB), so it is #N/A in every row; Q (actual capacity factor) is then 0 and W always takes the studies value R, and the CFOverride bounds S:T never act.
ref: Power tab rows 357-1635 (installed capacity by country and type, years 2000-2023 in F:AC). Q2999 = IFERROR(M2999/N2999,0) and W2999 = IF(AND(Q<T,Q>S),Q,R) then work as written.
effect: Egypt base year (prototype v4.10, same Power data): actual capacity factors gas 0.385 (studies 0.566), wind 0.436 (0.30), solar 0.347 (0.18), hydro 0.592 (0.432); oil stays at the studies 0.134 (actual 1.59 is above CFOverrideIfAbove). Base-year gas capacity (Y3000) 52.0 GW instead of 35.4 GW. Changes capacities, dispatch and investment in every year.

title: Autonomous efficiency gains use the price elasticity instead of the usage elasticity
why: Efficiency multiple = 1/(1+alpha+add)^(1+eps_F) with eps_F = row 3677 ("Price Elasticity").
ref: Documentation equation 3.4.2.3 and the fuel rows: exponent (1 + eps_U), eps_U = row 3676 ("Demand Elasticity").

title: Investment spending uses the capital cost at time factor 1
why: New investment (USD m) = $O2977 (base capital cost of table A2) x nameplate MW, ignoring the capital-cost time factor.

fixes.fill: L4276:AE4276, then fill L4276:AE4276 down to row 4284 (rows 3099-3107 line up with 4264-4272)

ref: Table A13 (rows 3099-3107 = capital cost x time factor), which the weighted-capex row 3181 already uses.
effect: 2040 total (row 4285) -18% (baseline) and -23% (carbon tax). Reporting only.

title: Investment logit normalised by the cheapest type, including types that may not be built
why: The logit weight is EXP(-K x cost / cheapest cost), with the cheapest taken over all nine types, including types not permitted (L3, rows 4061-4069).
ref: The permitted flags of table L3 (rows 4061-4069), already multiplied into rows 4073-4081. Change 4046 first, then 4045 (no circularity).
effect: No change in the baseline; carbon-tax run 2040 demand -0.07%, investment +0.3%.

title: Renewables take the world power parameters, never the country ones
why: Wind, solar, hydro, other renewables and biomass test IF(ISERROR(country), country, IF(ISERROR(world), world, ...)): the branches are inverted, so a valid country value is never taken and the world value (column M) always is. The four other types (rows 2977-2980) use IF(country>0, country, IF(world>0, world, ...)).

fixes.fill: P2981:T2985 (25 cells, one pattern: copy P2981 and paste into P2981:T2985)

ref: Rows 2977-2980, columns N:T of the same table (country value where > 0, else world). K2981:K2985 already fall back to the world row when the country has no row.
effect: Egypt: only solar has a country row (Power row 230): fixed O&M (Q2982) 11.831 instead of 15 $/kW/y; the studies WACC (S2982) 0.13 instead of 0.075, used only by the WACC source that takes the studies values (Egypt: Tech, so no effect); efficiency, variable O&M and lifetime are blank or 0 in the country row and stay at the world values.
note: P2981:T2985 are single-cell array formulas in the file (entered with Ctrl+Shift+Enter). Each INDEX returns one value, so the new formula can be entered normally or as an array formula; the result is the same.

title: Hydro investment always starts in the first year
why: H4067 = IF($L$3827>50%, FirstYearCalculations, NewInvHydYear): L3827 is the year header of table I5 (2022), so the test is always true and hydro may invest from the base year instead of from NewInvHydYear.
ref: The intended test is the base-year hydro share of generation (row 3846, L3846 = 6.7% for Egypt). The new formula takes it from table A4 (base-year power output, MWy), which equals L3846 and is data only, so no circularity; relative rows let the paste into the policy block read its own copy (rows 9315-9323).
effect: Egypt (hydro share 6.7% < 50%): hydro may invest only from NewInvHydYear = 2030. The legacy run invests in hydro in 2022-2029 (row 4257, new effective investment: 677 MWavg in total in the baseline, 1,015 MWavg in the carbon-tax run, policy row 10588); this goes to the other permitted types.

title: Capacity bought for this year's demand, although it comes online next year
why: New capacity bought in a year produces from the next year, but the need (row 4028 = MAX(row 4027 - row 4026, 0)) uses row 4027 "Next Year Demand" = L3752, this year's required generation; row 4031 "Actual effective generation in next year (should be the same)" shows the gap. The system enters every year one year of demand growth short.
ref: Row label of 4027. Next year's required generation is estimated as this year's x (1 + growth from last year to this year) (user decision 2026-10-20). Reading next year's demand itself (M3752) would make the workbook circular once a revenue that reads fuel use incl. power (the methane fee, rows 6136-6137, 8010) feeds the GDP feedback: next year's demand reads next year's GDP, which reads this year's revenue. The estimate reads only this and last year, so it is free of circular references in legacy and in the prototype (v6.2). K3752 in the first year: IFERROR gives growth 0.
effect: Egypt (legacy inputs, power_model_ref v6.2): installed capacity 77.9 GW in 2030 and 109.6 GW in 2040 against legacy 75.2 and 107.3 (next year's demand read directly, v4.14: 77.3 and 109.5). The estimate follows the demand shock (I92): the need is 4.3 GW in 2024 after the 2024 rebound and 0 in 2025.

title: Electricity producer subsidy compounds the factor and lags a year
why: From 2025 (column O) the projection is last year's value x last year's phase-out factor (O3601 = N3601 * N2213), so the factors multiply year on year and act a year late; row 3630 uses the base value $J3630 but last year's factor.
ref: Row 2213 = share of the original producer subsidy kept in the year. J3601 and J3630 hold the last historical value (2024, column N); row 3592 has no J cell, so its base is $N3592.
effect: None in the shipped Egypt runs (row 2213 = 1 in every year of both blocks). With a producer-subsidy phase-out (e.g. to 0 over 5 years) the legacy subsidy falls as the product of the factors and a year late; after the fix it follows the factor of the year (Egypt base: residential -0.097, industrial -0.021 $/kWh).

title: Regulations never reach power
why: The power shadow price per kWh reads only the feebate/ETS shadow price of power fuels (rows 2354, 2357, 2366). The regulation shadow price (general carbon price x EF when the policy is shadow pricing, D2369 = 1) is added for the fuel rows in 2377-2388 but never for power, although the energy efficiency regulation scenario covers power (F2403 = 1).
ref: Rows 2377 and 2380 (coal and gas power: IF($D$2369, L$2375 x EF, 0) + row 2354/2357). Row 2403 F = 1 when the shadow-pricing scenario covers power. I2354, I2357, I2366 = EF of coal, gas and oil in power.
effect: None in the shipped Egypt runs (explicit carbon tax, D2369 = 0). In a regulation scenario covering power, dispatch and investment see the shadow carbon price (the carbon-tax path) x EF. To measure: run "Energy efficiency regulations" before and after and compare rows 3412-3420 and the generation mix (rows 3828-3836).
note: Not via rows 2377/2380: their policy copies (8693-8704) keep the absolute references $D$2369 and L$2375, so in the policy block their regulation term reads the baseline general carbon price (L2375, 0 in the file); the new formulas use relative rows so the policy paste reads rows 8685, 8691 and 8719. The prototype also multiplies by the scenario's efficiency adjustment (0.7, Mitigation F86:F89); legacy's share C2371 is 0 (see L87), so it is left out here as in rows 2377-2388.

title: Cost of renewable subsidies counts the base subsidy twice, ignores the hydro switch and omits biomass
why: Rows 7883-7886 = (row 2743 + row 2745) x generation, but row 2745 already = row 2743 minus the additional subsidy, so the base subsidy enters twice; hydro (7885) ignores RenewableSubsidyHydro; the "Other renewables" row 7886 reads biomass generation (row 6298, not 6297); biomass has no row. Row 7889 enters total revenue (row 8009).

fixes.fill: D7887 (label; also E7887 = copy of E7886)
fixes.policy: D14203 = Biomass, E14203 = copy of E14202

ref: Table A17 (rows 3148-3152 = new subsidy per kWh by type, hydro only if RenewableSubsidyHydro = "Yes"), the same rows the engineer revenue memo 3665-3669 uses; generation by type rows 6294-6298.
effect: None in the shipped Egypt runs (no renewable subsidy: E2734 = E2735 = 0). With a subsidy, the cost falls by the double-counted base part and changes by the hydro switch and biomass.
note: Policy block: in legacy 465 the policy rows and the power rows they read both sit +6,316 below the baseline (L14199 = (L9059+L9061)*L12610*...), so a paste of the baseline row now works; the policy formulas are also given (in 456 a paste pointed 14 rows off). The elasticity-model memo rows 2947-2951 (shown by 7876-7880 only when the elasticity model is chosen) carry the same (L2743+L2745); change them the same way if that memo is used.

title: Long-term storage cost allocation (33%) applied twice
why: Row 3911 multiplies by $E3876 (33%) and row 3912 multiplies by $E3876 again.
ref: Example table on the same row, F3911:J3911 (= F3909*F3906); total row 3912 applies $E3876 once.
effect: None for Egypt (variable renewables below the long-term storage threshold).

title: Early coal retirement mixes nameplate and effective capacity
why: Row 3973 subtracts last year's non-coal retirement in nameplate MW (row 4004) from additions and demand growth in effective MW.
ref: Rows 4012-4019 (non-coal effective retirements, table K6). L3973 stays 0.
effect: None for Egypt (no coal).

title: Effective coal retirement is not capped like the nameplate retirement
why: Nameplate coal retirement (3994) is MIN(planned + early, capacity); the effective retirement (4011 = 4009 + 4010) is not capped.
ref: Rows 4012-4019 = nameplate x capacity factor. Rows 4009-4010 stay as memo rows.
effect: None for Egypt.

title: Feebate rebate per kWh consumed added to the cost per kWh generated
why: Rebate = -(row 3408) = -(cost per kWh generated / consumption-generation ratio 0.82), i.e. x1.22, but it is added to costs per kWh generated (rows 3412-3420).
ref: Rows 3412-3420 add the rebate to a cost per kWh generated, so the rebate must be per kWh generated (row 3407). Row 3408 becomes a memo row.
effect: None unless a power feebate is set (then the over-rebate of 22% goes).

title: Capacity needed is computed from last year's plan, not from actual capacity
why: M4024 = L4030 (last year's planned capacity), whether or not the investment could be placed.
ref: L4024 (base year) is actual effective capacity, SUMPRODUCT(capacity, capacity factor) = row 3753.
effect: None in the Egypt runs; matters only when scale-up limits leave a deficit.

title: Stray reference in dispatch
why: Required generation = MAX(required - other, $G4291 x total); G4291 is an empty, unrelated cell of table L21.
ref: Row meaning ("required generation", never negative).
effect: None while G4291 is empty.

title: Total nameplate investment row is zero
why: The total multiplies by $X3008, an empty cell, instead of summing the types.
ref: Total rows 4285 and 4003 of the same section.
effect: Row goes from 0 to the sum of the nine types. Nothing reads it.

title: China, Japan and Korea take regional power data
why: K2977 = IFERROR(MATCH(<iso>.mpp.<type>, Power!A25:A356, 0), world row). The regional block (Power rows 42-109) comes first and its codes chn.mpp.*, jpn.mpp.*, kor.mpp.* equal the country codes of China, Japan and Korea, so their regional rows are found instead of the country rows (Power rows 112-294).
ref: Power tab: country block A112:A294 (header row 111); +87 converts the position in that block to the position in A25:A356 that the INDEX formulas in N:T use. The world fallback L2977 is unchanged.
effect: None for Egypt (no regional row with its code). China, Japan, Korea: the country parameters replace the regional ones.

title: Countries without CoC risk data get Sri Lanka's WACC parameters
why: The real-WACC calculator (a LET formula) looks up each country's beta, equity risk premium, default spread, tax, equity weight and liquidity margin in rows 41-197 with XLOOKUP(..., if_not_found = $X$172), and row 172 is Sri Lanka. 47 countries of rows 202-390 have no row there (e.g. Afghanistan, Algeria, Iran, Myanmar, Nepal, Yemen, Zimbabwe) and silently get Sri Lanka's parameters (17.8% real WACC in 2022).

fixes.fill: CoC!D202:M390 (one pattern; easiest with Find and Replace limited to CoC!D202:M390: each ",$X$172)" by ",NA())" for X = H, F, D, G, I, J)

ref: Mitigation I2988:I2996 and AB2988:AB2996 already read CoC!D202:D390 inside IFERROR(..., 0.075), the default used for countries missing from CoC; with #N/A in the row they take it.
effect: None for Egypt (own row, 9.9% in 2022). The 47 countries take the 7.5% default (plus the technology premium with WACCSource = Tech) instead of Sri Lanka's 17.8%.
note: The cell text spans several lines (Alt+Enter). The #N/A of a country without data is itself the flag; the prototype also flags it on its Inputs sheet (PsCoCData).

title: Electricity consumer subsidy phased with the price-control factor; option text mismatch
why: With PowerSubsidyExemptInclude = "Include" the electricity consumer subsidy is multiplied by row 2216 (price-control phase-out factor) instead of row 2214 (consumer-subsidy phase-out factor). The unit text of MTInputs C138 says "Exempt/Include*" while the options (Dashboard L54) are "DoNotPhaseOut*" and "Include".
ref: Row 2214 (consumer factor, from YearConsSubPha and FFPhaseOut) as for the fuel consumer subsidies.
effect: None in the shipped Egypt runs (DoNotPhaseOut*, and J3606 = J3635 = 0: no consumer subsidy on electricity).

title: Power demand: efficiency increment sits on the net-exports row
why: Row 3719 carries two things: net-export data (D3719 = "Net Exports (Imports negative)", F:J) and, in the side table "Other Parameters", the power-demand efficiency increment (L3719 label, M3719 = M2198 = MTInputs F242). Nine demand rows of the engineer (H1) and elasticity (2823-2836) power models read it as $M3719, so the row reads as a trade term.

fixes.now: Additional Efficiency Improvements - Power demand | M3719: =M2198

ref: Row 2198 (table K2197:M2201, "Power" increment) already holds the value; rows 2199-2201 serve road, residential and industry the same way.
effect: None on values (the reference moves to the cell M3719 copies; F242 = 0 by default).
note: L2 changes the same cells M3691, M3697, M3703, M3709 ($F3677 -> $F3676); the two substitutions are independent, apply them in either order. Clearing L3719:M3719 is optional (cosmetic) once nothing reads M3719.

title: Renewable subsidy: start year of the additional subsidy reuses the consumer-subsidy phase-out year
where: Mitigation E2736 (policy E9052), row 270; MTInputs (new row)
why: E2736 "Year to add additional RE subsidy" = row 270 of the scenario = MTInputs F132 (YearConsSubPha), the year the consumer fuel subsidies start to be phased out; the additional renewable subsidy (MTInputs 353) has no start year of its own, and the label of row 276 says it starts in CPIntro.
ref: MTInputs rows 352-355 (renewable subsidy inputs) and the layout of each MTInputs row (D = scenario value, E = Dashboard, F = value used, G = default, H = name).
effect: None in the shipped runs (additional subsidy 0; the default start year 2027 equals today's YearConsSubPha). After the fix the two policies can be timed apart.
note: Fixed in legacy 465 by the CPAT team in its own way: E2736 reads a start-year input on the Dashboard (L57) through a defined name. The steps below were written for 456: Do first (otherwise E2736 shows #NAME?): append MTInputs row 416 after the last input row (413), copying row 356: B416 "New renewable energy subsidy, start year", C416 "year", D416 =INDEX($N416:$XAA416,1,_ScenarioToRun), E416 =Dashboard!$R$6 (a free cell next to the renewable-subsidy inputs P6:Q6; type 2027 there), F416 =IF(MTAct,D416,IF(CPATDefaultsOrUserDefined="Default",IF(I416="Y",E416,G416),E416)), G416 2027, H416 RenSubsidyAddStartYear, I416 "Y"; give scenario columns N416:XAA416 the values of N132:XAA132 where set; define the name RenSubsidyAddStartYear = MTInputs!$F$416 (workbook scope). Appending (not inserting) keeps every existing MTInputs row number. The prototype has the same input (MTInputs row 482, default 2027).

title: Capex decline options Low and Vhigh have no wind and solar series
why: RenewableCostDeclineRate Low builds the codes wld.ctf.low.wnd / .sol and Vhigh wld.ctf.vhg.wnd / .sol / .ore, which the Power tab (rows 303-330) does not hold (it has oldlow / oldvhg for wind and solar, and med.ore twice, rows 316 and 318). I3042 = IFERROR(MATCH(...),0) then gives 0 and INDEX(Power!F25:BE597, 0, year) in L3042:AE3046 errors.
ref: Power rows 323-330 (wld.ctf.oldlow/oldvhg.sol/wnd) and 316 (wld.ctf.med.ore). The prototype uses the same fallback (Inputs_ppath tcf|<type>|<option>): the older series of the same option for wind and solar, else Medium.
effect: None for Egypt (Medium*). With Low or Vhigh, the capex time factors of wind, solar (and other renewables under Vhigh) become the older series (Medium for other renewables) instead of errors.
note: The fallback is a choice: the user is to confirm it (the alternative is to add the missing series to the Power tab). Power row 318 is a second wld.ctf.med.ore, probably meant to be wld.ctf.vhg.ore. Decided (user 2026-10-19): the fallback is accepted; ask the CPAT team for the real Low and Vhigh series (data gap).

title: Power revenue rebate counts VAT that was never collected
why: The rebate per kWh (rows 3615, 3644) = rebate switch x carbon cost x pass-through x (1 + VAT), and row 3663 multiplies it by consumption into fiscal revenue (7874, then 7735 in the carbon-tax revenue). The VAT part of the carbon cost passed through is never collected (the VAT revenue row 3659 counts only the VAT on the price before policy), so the rebate returns VAT the government never had.
ref: Rows 3611 and 3640 (VAT rates). The price rows 3614-3617 are unchanged: users still see the carbon cost and its VAT removed; only the fiscal rebate excludes the VAT.
effect: None in the shipped Egypt runs (rebate off, J3595 = 0). With PowerRebates on, the rebate revenue falls by the VAT share: residential x 1/1.149 (VAT 14.9%), industrial unchanged (VAT 0).

title: Manual electricity excise revenue counts the whole excise, also where the price does not include it
why: Row 3660 = manual excise (rows 3602, 3631) x consumption in every year. The price includes the excise only through the change of the sum of components since the last historical year (2024, column N) times the pass-through (rows 3607 and 3610), and not at all up to 2024, where the price is data.
ref: Row 3594 (year), I3600 (last historical year, 2024), N3602 / N3631 (excise in 2024), row 3596 (pass-through, the same for both groups).
effect: None in the shipped Egypt runs (AdditionalExcise off, D199 = 0). With a manual excise, the revenue memo (and row 7762, the excise revenue by fuel) counts only the excise in the price: 0 up to 2024, then pass-through x the change since 2024.

title: Fuel price for power averages later years
why: The fuel price for power is AVERAGE(t-2 .. t+2) of the fuel prices (rows 3072-3080): this year's power costs read the next two years. Safe only while those prices depend on inputs alone; a quantity-dependent price would make the workbook circular through the GDP feedback.
ref: Trailing 5-year average (this year and the 4 before; fewer in the first years), user decision 2026-10-20 (no formula reads a later year). The L-column 'now' text follows the pattern of P3155 and Q3155 (decoded from the .xlsb); check L:O before pasting.
effect: Price changes reach power costs about two years later than in legacy. Not recalculated in Excel; the prototype v6.2 quick check reports the change.

title: Levelised variable cost reads the variable cost to 2041
why: Investment choices levelise the variable cost from the year to the end of the horizon (perfect foresight). Safe only while that cost is built from inputs alone; a variable cost that reads quantities (e.g. a solved ETS price that depends on emissions) would make the workbook circular.
ref: No cell change today: rows 3439-3447 levelise input-driven costs (fuel prices, variable O&M, policy rates). Rule: keep them input-driven; if the ETS price becomes endogenous, levelise the announced (input) price path, not the solved one.
effect: None today (latent).
